national.summary: Pennsylvania's outbreak is the largest in the country​, with over 1,600 cases reported, and the deaths this year are the Keystone State's first from measles in 35 years.
national.body: Pennsylvania on Monday announced its ninth measles-related death this year as cases continue to surge across the U.S., reaching their highest mark in decades.The death was reported in Centre County, in the middle of the state. The Pennsylvania Department of Health did not provide any further information about the patient. The announcement came just three days after Virginia reported that a child under the age of 5 had died after testing positive for measles. It was Virginia's first measles-related death this year, the state's Health Department said.Pennsylvania's outbreak is the largest in the country, with over 1,600 cases reported, according to the state Department of Health, and the deaths this year are the Keystone State's first from measles in 35 years.In Lancaster County, one woman told CBS News her three children all have measles.The U.S. had eliminated measles by the year 2000, but last week the country lost that status. A country is considered to have eliminated measles if there are "no locally transmitted measles infections or outbreaks lasting 12 months or longer," according to the World Health Organization.Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data show that about a quarter of this year's measles cases are linked to outbreaks that began in 2025, when the U.S. saw a 30-year high of 2,289 cases, and that the virus continued to spread. As of last week, there have been 5,838 confirmed measles cases in the U.S. this year, according to the CDC. Dr. Evan Shirey, an infectious disease specialist, said he went from seeing no measles cases to dealing with them "almost every day."He blames misinformation for vaccine hesitancy."The manifestations of that can just be horrible to see," he said. "Children gasping for air. Seeing a child who is altered, confused, unable to recognize their own mom."Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has long been criticized for casting doubt on vaccine safety, said in the wake of the U.S. losing its measles elimination status, "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles."Kindergarten vaccination rates have fallen below the 95% needed to protect the immunocompromised and infants too young to be vaccinated. It marked the latest attack in the North African nation tied to the Russia-Ukraine war. Zelenskyy said Monday in a social media post that Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones in the operation, which sank a Russian corvette. The Ukrainian leader described the ship as one of Russia's newest vessels commissioned in 2023 during Russia's invasion."Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk," he wrote. He added that a Ka-27 military helicopter was destroyed in the attack. "We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. Yet in reversing itself, Nvidia is undermining its own corporate code of conduct and could expose the company to potential legal liability, Charles Elson, founding director of the John L. national.title: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after affair with alleged spy as Trump says 'I made the deal'
national.summary: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
national.body:
Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

The company had come under pressure from Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to reverse course and bring Huang back.

But Democrats have accused the Trump administration of selling out national security for financial gain. Huang is due to testify before Congress in early December.

His comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that had left the S&P 500 in correction territory.

Stock prices for Nvidia fell sharply after Huang stepped down, but jumped by 31% after he was reappointed on Monday - adding about $1tn to the company's market value.

But Nvidia's closing price was still down slightly from its Friday morning opening price.

Board Chairman Harvey C Jones said in a statement earlier in the day: "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."

The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

national.summary: Military spouses interviewed by PBS News say there is more to do to improve quality of life for military families.
national.body:
One thing Haley Harman learned quickly as a military spouse stationed overseas is that the commissary "is not the place to go for produce."

She and her husband have been stationed in both South Korea and Japan in their four years of marriage. In both places, "a lot of the items that are sent to the base arrive expired since it's being shipped from the states."

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

She learned many seek produce from local farmers off base. But transportation options can be limited; the base where Harman is stationed only authorizes one vehicle per family. And many families, including Harman's, also rely on U.S. food assistance, which isn't redeemable at off-base markets or grocery stores.

"We are on WIC (the USDA's Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children). My husband is 10 years into his career and an E6" — a midlevel enlisted position — "and we still qualify," Harman said. "I can't think of any other career where you work for 10 years and you still qualify for food assistance."

Harman is among the more than 1.4 million spouses and dependents of active duty U.S. military service members around the world. Issues with housing, employment, childcare and healthcare can greatly affect quality of life.

These challenges have long been well known within the military community, and while legislative efforts have addressed some of them, spouses interviewed by PBS News say there is more to do to improve quality of life for military families.

In nearly a dozen interviews and more than 230 responses to a callout from PBS News, military spouses highlighted maintaining employment as one of the biggest challenges they've faced, with more than half of all responses referencing the issue. Also cited: challenges navigating the Exceptional Family Members Program, meant to support family members with special medical or educational needs, and the financial burdens of permanent change of station (PCS) moves.

national.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
national.summary: Megaspeed has been accused of funneling AI chips to China after a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang became public.
national.body:
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.

The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.

The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.

The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.

When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.

Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.

Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.

China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

national.summary: Jimmy Gomez, who lost his election this month and only serving in the House until the year's end, was accused of sexual misconduct with a staff member.
national.body:
US Representative Jimmy Gomez has said he will resign from Congress after an ethics committee said it found credible evidence that he engaged in sexual misconduct, according to CBS News.

A report released on Monday by the House Ethics Committee stated that Gomez, a California Democrat, made "unwelcome sexual advances" towards a House staff member, "disregarding the power imbalance" between them.

Gomez, 51, said he disagreed with the report's findings but would resign on 1 December. The five-term congressman lost his seat representing part of Los Angeles in the midterm elections this month and was set to leave the House at the end of the year.

Gomez said in a statement on Monday that he had "strong disagreements" with the committee's findings, but that he saw "no other alternative than to resign", according to CBS, the BBC's US media partner.

He added: "I recognize the seriousness of the Ethics Committee's report and as I previously stated I take full responsibility for the personal mistakes I committed outside of my marriage."

The panel originally investigated a report that Gomez had been seen kissing a younger staffer at a party hosted by then-Congressman Eric Swalwell. That report came shortly after Swalwell, also a California Democrat, resigned over sexual misconduct allegations of his own.

The bipartisan committee announced its investigation into Gomez, who is married, in August, after lawyers for the House staffer accused him of inappropriate sexual contact. He had maintained at the time that while he had made mistakes, his actions were consensual.

The ethics committee interviewed a woman, referred to only as "Witness 1" in the report, who said the congressman made unwanted sexual advances toward her on two occasions, once in public and once in his congressional office, while she was a House staffer.

The U.S. Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels of unstable lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday is expected to produce a plume of dust containing lead particles that could extend as far as 100 miles away, a plan that residents , lawmakers and environmental groups say was not communicated appropriately.

The date of the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, has changed several times as a result of court challenges, which in part contend that the government failed to adequately warn local communities about environmental and health risks.

Lead is a toxic metal that can cause severe health problems, particularly for children and people who are pregnant. No amount of lead exposure is safe, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention .

Originally scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, the detonation was initially moved to Monday, the latest the Army said the event could happen before dropping temperatures threatened to further destabilize the degrading lead azide.

A federal appeals court on Friday temporarily suspended the Army's permit for the detonation as a federal judge considers a lawsuit brought by environmental groups seeking to block the blast.

The Justice Department said the Army is invoking its emergency powers that allow it to move forward with the explosion without the Environmental Protection Agency's permit.

national.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump a path to erasing hush money conviction
national.summary: The decision moves the case to a federal court, where Trump could seek to have charges dismissed on immunity grounds.
national.body:
Michael Sisak, Associated Press Michael Sisak, Associated Press

NEW YORK (AP) — A federal appeals court on Monday gave President Donald Trump a new pathway to erasing his hush money criminal conviction, moving the case to a federal court where he could seek to have it dismissed on immunity grounds.

A three-judge panel of the 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision that had kept the case in state court in New York, where Trump was tried and convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court. If that happens, Trump could then argue that verdict should be discarded because of presidential immunity.

The decision also set in motion a halt to proceedings in Trump's simultaneous state court appeal. Trump denies wrongdoing and was given no punishment in the case, which made him the first U.S. president convicted of a crime.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein's earlier denial of Trump's request to move the historic case from state court to federal court, a process known as removal.

The appellate judges ruled that Hellerstein "erred in holding that removal is categorically unavailable in a state criminal case" after a conviction and erred in denying that Trump had good cause to make two attempts at moving the case — once after his indictment and again after his trial.

Tech stocks more broadly have also rallied following large falls on Friday , with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang's return was announced.

Tesla shares also lept up by nearly 11.5%, while other tech gains were more muted by comparison: Amazon shares were up nearly 3.5%, and Apple and Microsoft rose by less than 2%.

national.title: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
national.summary: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.
national.body:
Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't.

The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi , co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?

The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch.

Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes , has called it "a dangerous escalation".

It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism.

Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga.

Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks – what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" – have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia.

The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.

national.title: Trump orders US military not to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa without court approval
national.summary: The US Army had said it planned to detonate the explosives on Wednesday despite a court-ordered pausea as public outcry intensified.
national.body:
President Donald Trump said he has ordered the US army not to move ahead with plans to detonate five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa on Wednesday until a court rules on the issue.

The administration previously had planned to go forward with the plans despite legal challenges and public outcry over the potential health risks to nearby communities.

A court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation.

"I feel the proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward," Trump said, referencing the court that halted the detonation.

He added in his post on Truth Social that the US had "an opportunity to do a highly controlled detonation of these dangerous and rapidly corroding materials" because of optimal weather.

Even after the court pause ordered on Thursday, the justice department told the court that the army intends to move forward with its plan, because of an "immediate risk" that those materials could "spontaneously explode".

Environmental groups have accused the government of skirting the judicial process.

Lead azide is a highly volatile compound used as a detonator. Earlier this year, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) found that the material had degraded over time to the point where it was now too risky to move the material, according to Iowa Public Radio.

national.title: Trump says Army will not detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa without court approval
national.summary: President Donald Trump says he will defer to a federal appeals court on whether to proceed with detonating degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant.
national.body:
Susan Montoya Bryan, Associated Press Susan Montoya Bryan, Associated Press

President Donald Trump on Monday said he will defer to a federal appeals court on whether the administration moves ahead with plans to detonate several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant.

The detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide was initially planned for Friday, but the Army has since changed the date three times following an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects. They had planned for a detonation on Wednesday, saying the weather was most favorable that day.

The Army had no immediate comment when asked about the president's social media post. Environmentalists sued last week in an effort to stop the detonation, winning a stay from the appeals court pending a decision on the validity of an emergency permit approved by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency that cleared the way for the operation. Trump said he prefers to take care of the volatile material as soon as possible and that a controlled detonation would be much safer. "At the same time, have ordered the military not to do so until such time as the 8th Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Gov.-elect Rob Sand agreeing to the operation," Trump said in a statement. If Sand and the court don't agree, Trump said the administration will have no choice but to not proceed with the planned detonation, adding that he would hold the incoming governor responsible for "any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation."

Sand said in a social media post on Sunday that because of previous decisions that have already been made, "No good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been."

He questioned why a contract to remove the explosive risk was canceled, why nothing was done and "why we are rushing to demolition now in late November."

"The safety of Iowans should be the top priority of everyone involved," he said. "All relevant federal, state and local government resources should be focused on protecting everyone that could be impacted."

Some residents near Middletown, where the ammunition plant is located, have been sealing their windows and doors as a precaution to keep out any lead dust that might result from the detonation. Others who live farther away were raising concern on social media about the possible paths that the plume could take depending on shifts in the wind.

national.title: Senate leadership vote tests newly elected Democrats' promise of change
national.summary: The Democratic Party's incoming senators face an early test of their campaign promises to shake up Washington as they decide who will lead their new majority.
national.body:
Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Democratic Party's incoming senators haven't even been sworn into office yet, but the decision over who will lead their new majority is already testing the promise of change they made as candidates.

The 13 new Democrats are part of the largest incoming Senate class in decades, with several winning in Republican strongholds by promising to shake up Washington and be independent voices. Now they are caught up in a classic insider fight, forced to decide whether to stick with longtime Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York or back challenger Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.

Newly elected progressives, including Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, have backed Van Hollen, who is taking on Schumer with promises of a more aggressive legislative approach. Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who is returning to Washington after losing his seat in 2024, supports Schumer.

But the incoming senators from traditionally Republican states such as Texas, Mississippi, Iowa and South Carolina, whose victories helped deliver Democrats the majority, have so far largely avoided taking sides publicly. Annie Andrews of South Carolina has said she is talking with both candidates. Scott Colom of Mississippi says he wants to get to know them better before deciding and describes himself as being in "listening mode."

Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton said Thursday he would not back Schumer, but declined to endorse anyone.

"I'm looking for someone who is going to bring people together," Hamilton told MSNow. "Right now, in places like Kansas, there's a lot of people who don't feel that in Chuck Schumer."

Schumer's long-standing relationships and knowledge of Senate machinery are a big advantage heading into the Dec. 1 vote, which will be held by secret ballot. He also oversees Senate Democrats' campaign spending group, funneling millions into many of the races and, in some cases, recruiting the candidates to run in the first place.

national.title: WATCH: Trump delivers address on Newsom's move to grant clemency for California's death row
national.summary: The White House said the speech would be about protecting American families and Newsom's decision to commute the death sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life without parole.
national.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump is set to condemn California Gov. Gavin Newsom's clemency to the state's death row inmates in a speech at the Justice Department on Monday, his second address in less than two years at an agency that has moved aggressively to fulfill his White House's agenda and pursue criminal cases against his adversaries.

The White House said the speech, in the building's ceremonial Great Hall, would be about protecting American families and Newsom's decision to commute the death sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life without parole.

But it was unclear to what extent the address would also function as a forum for the Republican president to again encourage the prosecution of his political opponents and revisit years-old grievances about a Justice Department that has repeatedly investigated him over the past decade.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Newsom earlier this month said he will change more than 500 death sentences in his state to life in prison without the possibility of parole. The Democratic governor, who frequently trades barbs with Trump and is considering a run for president, said the decision was among the most difficult choices of his career because it will surface painful memories for crime victims' families.

Trump's speech is unfolding against the backdrop of sweeping Republican losses in midterm elections this month that gave Democrats control of Congress and that tee up possible House and Senate investigations over everything from the mass firings of agents and prosecutors who investigated Trump to a series of politically charged investigations by the Trump administration Justice Department that have been rejected by grand juries and judges alike.

Trump's sway over the department is embodied by a banner of his face that hangs outside the building's exterior, an indication of what critics say is the erosion of the institution's historic independence.

Trump will be joined by Attorney General Todd Blanche, his former personal defense lawyer, who has been unapologetic in his view that the president is entitled to exert his will on the Justice Department. Blanche was elevated from deputy attorney general to the top job in April after Trump ousted Pam Bondi, who struggled to satisfy the president's demands for retribution and endured bipartisan criticism over the handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

national.title: Writers unhappy with PEN America's response to war in Gaza form new chapter
national.summary: Novelist Maaza Mengiste says they don't seek rivalry with PEN America but differ in structure and priorities.
national.body:
Hillel Italie, Associated Press Hillel Italie, Associated Press

NEW YORK (AP) — Ta-Nehisi Coates, M. Gessen and Jacqueline Woodson are among more than 100 writers, editors, agents and others in the literary community seeking to establish a chapter of PEN that is independent from PEN America, the longtime free expression organization that has endured tensions with various members in recent years over the war in Gaza and other issues.

The new group, called PEN Writes US, would be "guided by the PEN Charter's vision of 'one humanity, living in peace and equality in one world,'" Monday's announcement by the proposed organization reads.

Novelist Maaza Mengiste told The Associated Press during a recent telephone interview that PEN Writes does not seek to be a rival of PEN America and will likely share common ground about fighting censorship and oppression and encouraging discussions among writers. But she did say that PEN Writes will differ in its structure and in some of its priorities, ideally becoming "a center where sustained and equal advocacy for all writers guides principles, rather than institutional caution."

Numerous writers and activists have been unhappy with PEN America's response to the war in Gaza, contending that PEN America has been reluctant to criticize Israel or to defend the rights of Palestinian writers with the same force it has advocated for writers elsewhere.

"I think there's been a feeling for quite a while that PEN's response to the war in Gaza has been inadequate," says PEN Writes member Francine Prose, a former president of PEN America.

Fallout from the war in Gaza led PEN America to call off its annual awards show and "World Voices" festival in 2024 because so many participants dropped out. (Those events resumed in 2025 and 2026). Last summer, PEN America President Dinaw Mengestu resigned after PEN published a report about obstacles and harassment faced by Israeli and Jewish writers since the war began in 2023.

Mengestu, a prize-winning novelist who is now a member of PEN Writes, at the time cited the report's criticism of cultural boycotts and expressed support for the Palestinian-led boycott, divestment and sanctions movement, or BDS. Organizers advocate economic and cultural pressure on Israel to end the country's occupation of territories captured in the 1967 Mideast war, grant full equality to Arab citizens of Israel and promote the rights of Palestinian refugees to return.

local.title: Piling up: Buffalo has no contractor to dispose of leaves
local.summary: The city is currently without a contractor to dispose of the leaves residents collect, bag and set out on the curbside for crews to collect.
local.body: Buffalo does not have a way to dispose of leaves and the problem is piling up in a parking lot in North Buffalo. The city is currently without a contractor to dispose of the leaves residents collect, bag and set out on the curbside for crews to collect. Instead, the bags end up in a pile at the NFTA's LaSalle Station parking lot in North Buffalo. Buffalo's Deputy Mayor Benjamin Swanekamp tells me the pile is a holding station for the bags before being transported to a holding garage in South Buffalo. "Right now we have to either find a contractor willing to work with us, or as might be increasingly necessary, us to develop our own yard waste recycling program," Swanekamp said.The leaves were once dealt with by Geiter Done, a yard waste disposal company based in the Seneca Babcock neighborhood. But in 2024, the company was issued a notice of violation by the DEC after odor complaints. As a result, Swanekamp tells me the Buffalo Common Council did not approve a contract renewal with the company."When it came up for renewal, the Common Council rejected them two years in a row, so since then the city's been in the position of having to hold debris," Swanekamp said.So why doesn't the city just send all of this to a landfill? New York state regulations prohibit leaves and certain yard waste from being sent to landfills to prevent methane emissions. Methane is a greenhouse gas that has been shown to drive rapid climate warming.The city has not yet been able to find another contractor who will take the leaves, even after putting out a request for qualifications to find a suitable vendor."We were hoping to get a partner on this, we're gonna have to continue working the phones. If that doesn't happen, we'll have to continue building the capability and scale right within city government," Swanekamp said.The Town of Tonawanda handles its own leaf collection and disposal in-house. Residents are asked to put loose leaves at the curbside during a certain time frame before crews vacuum them up. Swanekamp says Buffalo is looking to emulate that method in the future.Despite the problem, Swanekamp says residents should continue to follow the city's instructions when it comes to leaf collection — gathering them and putting them in clear or paper bags and placing them on the curbside for city crews to come and get. local.title: Holiday shopping rush brings increased concerns about package theft and scams
local.summary: Americans are expected to spend a record $275 billion shopping online this holiday season, creating plenty of opportunities for thieves and scammers.
local.body: With Black Friday just days away, the holiday shopping rush is about to kick into high gear. Americans are expected to spend a record $275 billion shopping online this holiday season, creating plenty of opportunities for thieves and scammers.A study by SafeWise estimates that more than 100 million packages were stolen nationwide in 2025. While that's down from the previous year, porch piracy remains a major concern.Meanwhile, the Federal Trade Commission says fake package delivery notifications are the most commonly reported type of text message scam.Amazon, the nation's largest online retailer, is preparing for the holiday rush by hiring more than 300,000 workers nationwide."This is our Super Bowl," Amazon spokesperson Owen Torres told 7 News.The company is offering advice to help customers protect their purchases.One recommendation is to take advantage of Amazon's package tracking tools, which allow customers to monitor deliveries and share tracking information with friends or family members who can retrieve packages if the customers aren't home.Customers can also provide specific delivery instructions, including asking drivers to leave packages in less visible locations."I kind of have the instructions to hide it behind one of my planters," Torres said. "It takes it away from street view and protects the packages out of sight."If a package is stolen, Amazon recommends reporting the theft to local police before contacting customer service through the Amazon app or website to explore possible remedies.Package theft isn't the only concern.Amazon says approximately 360,000 customers contact the company each year to ask whether an email, text message or phone call claiming to be from Amazon is legitimate.The company warns that scammers often create a sense of urgency, request personal information or demand payments through gift cards.Amazon recently introduced a new tool for its "Alexa for Shopping" AI assistant, which allows customers to ask whether a suspicious communication actually came from the company. Customers can access the feature through the Amazon app or Amazon.com.Amazon also recommends using its secure Locker delivery locations as an alternative to having packages left unattended on doorsteps.

local.title: 'Our last 8 months have been a living hell': 4 indicted in JohnLuc Jubert's death
local.summary: Eight months after 30-year-old JohnLuc Jubert was killed in a crash on the Kensington Expressway, four people have been indicted on manslaughter charges.
local.body: Eight months after 30-year-old JohnLuc Jubert was killed in a crash on the Kensington Expressway, four people have been indicted on manslaughter charges. On the night of March 19, Jubert was driving on Route 33, heading home after dropping off boxes at the apartment he and his girlfriend, Katelyn Baran, were preparing to move into, when he encountered traffic at a standstill.Authorities said as many as 50 drivers were participating in a drag racing event on the Kensington Expressway."They completely ignored the rules of the roadway, shutting down the flow of traffic on a major expressway," Erie County District Attorney Michael Keane said.Keane said participants were blocking lanes, doing burnouts, setting off fireworks and driving at speeds of 100 mph.Prosecutors allege three men, 23-year-old Shafi Ahmed, 21-year-old Saif Junab Ali and 21-year-old Abu Saleh, blocked all three lanes of the expressway, leaving Jubert caught in the traffic.A fourth driver, who was 17 at the time, then approached at an "extremely high rate of speed" while trying to avoid a vehicle in front of him."He swerved, and he struck Mr. Jubert's vehicle directly from behind," Keane said.All four defendants have now been charged with second-degree manslaughter. They are additionally charged with leaving the scene of an incident resulting in death.The indictments come after months of waiting for Jubert's family and friends, who have called for those responsible to be held accountable."What they did to my brother, to my parents' son, to Katelyn's soulmate, what they did to our entire life, it's unfathomable what they did," Jubert's brother, Daniel Jubert, said.Baran said the past eight months have been devastating."Our last eight months have been a living hell," she said.Baran said she believes everyone who contributed to the circumstances surrounding the fatal crash should be held responsible."They all made this tragedy happen," she said. local.title: 'It can be frustrating for people': Air travelers weigh in on recent flight delays and disruptions
local.summary: As recent delays and a Delta outage rattle holiday plans, travelers at the Buffalo Niagara International Airport share their worries — but officials say operations are back to normal.
local.body: As recent delays and a Delta outage rattle holiday plans, travelers at the Buffalo Niagara International Airport share their worries — but officials say operations are back to normal.Recent flight delays have travelers heading home for Thanksgiving weekend worried about their journeys.I caught up with Emma Lipshultz as she arrived from Miami, flying alone for the first time with her 3-month-old daughter. She came to see her dad, who lives in Orchard Park. But with weeks of flight delays and Sunday's Delta outage, she was nervous about traveling for Thanksgiving."I definitely was nervous about that, but we were very happy that we made it," Lipshultz said.Her return trip is also on her mind."We're going back on Sunday, which is again a busy time to fly, so I'm a little bit nervous about that," Lipshultz said.Another traveler, headed home to Kansas City on a Delta flight after a conference in Canada, is also worrying about the recent flight disruptions."I heard horror stories about my colleagues and other friends who were traveling, and it's just pretty crazy when things like that happen," Dithi Banerjee said.Banerjee said the impact goes beyond passengers."It's not just the passengers. I feel for the airport employees. I feel for the airline employees, who really have to face the brunt of all of the anxiety and the disappointment," Banerjee said.NFTA spokesperson Kelly Khatib tells me operations at the Buffalo airport have been back to normal."Anytime that anyone's travel plans or wherever you're going is interrupted, it can be frustrating for people, but I think the biggest thing that people should remember is air travel is the safest way to go," Khatib stated. "You could be traveling out of the Buffalo airport, and everything is a-okay, but when you get to your second destination, if you have a stop in between, that might be different."The best advice if you're flying: download your airline's app and carry on your luggage if you can. No matter where you're headed, it's always advised to arrive at least an hour and a half early.WATCH: 'It can be frustrating for people': Air travelers weigh in on recent flight delays and disruptionsThis story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.title: High Falls to light orange for domestic violence awareness
local.summary: The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.
local.body:
The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.

"There isn't always closure for a lot of women, and so by calling attention to this, we're hoping that people will just be more aware, and that women who perhaps are victims will feel more empowered to get out of the situation that they are in," says Bonnie Abrams, a past president and current advocacy co-chair at Zonta Club.

A 2025 report shows domestic violence incidents in the City of Rochester are 2.4 times higher than the statewide rates, and the Monroe County rates are nearly double the state numbers, according to the Willow Domestic Violence Center.

"Though domestic violence occurs on all social strata, you know, but I think that unfortunately there are more incidents because of people feeling powerless, and I think that that's perhaps one of the reasons that the statistics are higher here in Rochester, and that's another reason why we want to call attention to this issue," she explained.

Abrams says the word "Zonta" comes from the Lakota word meaning "honest" or "trustworthy". She says she wants everyone to know there are trusted people willing to help.

The Rochester branch is part of a national network that first started in Buffalo. They issue grants and other support to organizations that further its mission to improve the lives of women and girls.

The falls lighting will kick off the club's 16 Days of Activism that runs through Human Rights Day on December 10th.

The event starts at Genesee Brew House at 5 p.m. Participants will walk over for the falls lighting and a proclamation reading from Mayor Malik Evans' office. A local survivor of domestic violence will serve as speaker.

local.summary: As fans around the country say goodbye to the late Fiona, the San Antonio Zoo paid special tribute to the beloved hippo with a goodbye letter from her long-distance "boyfriend" Timothy.
local.body: As fans around the country say goodbye to the late Fiona, who stole America's hearts in 2017 after she was born prematurely at the Cincinnati Zoo, the San Antonio Zoo paid special tribute to the beloved hippo with a goodbye letter from her long-distance "boyfriend" Timothy.It wasn't long after Fiona's first birthday that she received her first big dating request from Timothy the hippo in San Antonio. "I have seen your pictures and videos on the internet at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden and I think you are the most beautiful hippopotamus I have ever seen," a post from the San Antonio Zoo, dated March, 6, 2018, reads. "Perhaps we can meet someday and be boyfriend and girlfriend?"Just a few day's later, Timothy's post got a response from Fiona. "Fiona thinks you’re cute too, but it’s what’s on the inside that really counts!" the Cincinnati Zoo posted in response. From there, their relationship took off.While the hippos were never able to meet in person, they carried on a "long-distance relationship" for years, with Timothy sending Fiona gifts and making special posts on her birthday. It was far from a one-sided romance. Fiona even sent Timothy a "kiss" for his birthday in 2021. "Your kiss painting that you sent me was my fav!" the zoo posted after Timothy received Fiona's gift. "Thank you so much and remember I always think you are the most beautiful hippo I’ve ever seen!"Just like so many treasured love stories, Timothy and Fiona's has a tragic ending. Fiona died on Thursday after swallowing a hat that accidentally got into her enclosure. She was just 9 years old.After the news of Fiona's death spread, the San Antonio Zoo posted a special goodbye tribute to the beloved hippo from her biggest admirer, Timothy. local.title: Leaders Made Here: How Western New York Maritime Charter School is shaping Buffalo's future
local.summary: Through a combination of academics, character development, physical fitness and leadership training, the school is preparing students to become confident, responsible leaders.
local.body: At Western New York Maritime Charter School, education goes far beyond the classroom. Through a combination of academics, character development, physical fitness and leadership training, the school is preparing students to become confident, responsible leaders.Serving students in grades 5 through 12, Maritime incorporates military-inspired structure through its Naval Junior Reserve Officers Training Corps (NJROTC) program. Cadets are encouraged to take responsibility, support their peers and develop skills that will serve them long after graduation.The school's guiding philosophy, "Leaders Made Here," is more than just a motto."I went from a cadet who was not on the best track at Maritime, and I had all the tools given to me to become someone better," said Cameron Barclay, the school's Cadet Commanding Officer.Maritime's approach emphasizes hands-on leadership, accountability and personal growth, giving students opportunities to challenge themselves while preparing for college, military service or careers in the workforce.The school's impact also extends into the community. According to their website, cadets completed more than 9,400 hours of community service during the 2025–2026 school year, while the Class of 2026 achieved a 94% graduation rate."What it comes down to is, can we make you a better citizen once you graduate from this school?" said Antony Washington, Master Sergeant in the United States Marine Corps. "We teach life skills, right? And that's exactly what most people need when they graduate from high school."Through education, mentorship and leadership opportunities, Western New York Maritime Charter School continues to demonstrate its mission is about more than preparing students for graduation. local.title: This flu season is already way ahead of last year's pace
local.summary: With the holidays quickly approaching, health officials are urging people to get vaccinated.
local.body:
Flu season is already off to a fast and aggressive start both statewide and in Greater Rochester.

As of Nov. 14, Monroe County has reported 1,259 confirmed cases of influenza, more than six times the number of cases that were reported last year at this time.

There are also 129 flu-related hospitalizations and fewer than 10 flu-related deaths. State and county data trackers do not provide an exact number of deaths until the number exceeds 10.

In a virtual news conference Monday afternoon, Monroe County Commissioner of Public Health Dr. Marielena Vélez de Brown stressed the importance of vaccination.

"The vaccine may not prevent every infection, but it can certainly reduce your chances of getting very sick and lower your risk of ending up in the hospital," she said.

Monroe County's current flu vaccination rate is 26.5%, higher than the statewide rate of 22%.

The flu vaccine is recommended to everyone beginning at 6 months of age.

"With the holidays approaching, many of us will be traveling, gathering indoors, and spending time with family and friends," Vélez de Brown said. "So, getting vaccinated isn't just about protecting your own health; it's also about protecting the people you're gathering with."

local.title: Coalition calls on Hochul and legislators to increase upstate transit funding
local.summary: Transit advocates, elected officials, business leaders, and transit users say the state isn't providing enough money for an essential service.
local.body:
Transportation advocates, elected officials, and community leaders are calling on Gov. Kathy Hochul and legislative leaders to increase state funding for upstate public transit systems.

State Sen. Jeremy Cooney, who chairs the Senate's transportation committee, is among them. Speaking at a news conference Monday, he said that when services are disrupted, it affects the users who rely on it.

"Public transportation in New York is not a luxury," Cooney said. "It is a necessity that connects people to essential services like medical appointments, to work, to school, to childcare, to so much more. It's also a bridge to economic opportunities and economic mobility."

The Rochester area is currently preparing for the latest disruption to transit service.

RTS announced earlier this month that it was shutting down its On Demand service next year to help bridge a budget gap. The transit service faces a $30 million structural deficit that officials have said is fueled by costs that are growing faster than revenue.

Local News RTS ending its On Demand service next year Jeremy Moule Regional Transit Service instead plans to restructure service in affected areas, to include expansion of some fixed routes. The On Demand service launched in 2021 as part of a major overhaul of RTS routes. It used smaller buses and vans and was intended as a flexible way to fill gaps created by the elimination of some suburban routes. local.summary: Rochester firefighters arrived to find heavy smoke and flames on the third floor of the sprawling former camera manufacturing complex.
local.body:
The former Kodak Hawkeye building on St. Paul Street became the scene of a massive fire Sunday night.

Rochester firefighters arrived to find heavy smoke and flames on the third floor of the sprawling former camera manufacturing complex.

Lt. Howard Villegas of the Rochester Fire Department said large amounts of stored materials helped fuel the blaze and made it difficult to extinguish.

“There was a lot of cardboard, and cardboard boxes filled with several items," Villegas said.

A firefighter was taken to the hospital for observation and is expected to make a full recovery with no significant injuries.

Villegas also stated, “it seemed that any occupants may have exited the structure prior to our arrival, but this was what was witnessed by bystanders.”

Crews advanced multiple hose lines, ventilated the building, and worked to stop the fire from spreading. Despite challenging conditions inside the multi-story building, crews were able to keep most of the damage confined to the third floor, according to the department.

local.body:
Empire State Development on Monday announced the completion of Ultrapak, LLC's expansion and modernization project at its long-term facility in the city of Dunkirk.

Supported by up to $120,000 in performance-based Excelsior Jobs Program tax credits, the completed $800,000 project integrates advanced equipment to increase domestic production and reduce reliance on offshore manufacturing. As a result of this infrastructure expansion, Ultrapak has committed to creating 10 new skilled jobs in Western New York as manufacturing output increases.

"Under Gov. (Kathy) Hochul's leadership, New York State continues to strengthen its position as a global manufacturing powerhouse," said Empire State Development President, CEO & Commissioner Hope Knight. "The completion of Ultrapak's expansion in Dunkirk is a direct result of her commitment to investing in the high-tech equipment and infrastructure local businesses need to scale. Alongside major regional anchors like Cummins Jamestown Engine Plant and Wells Enterprises, this project is fueling sustained economic growth and supporting a dedicated workforce in Western New York."

Since 1987, Ultrapak has been manufacturing heat-shrinkable sleeves which are used as decorative labels, tamper-evidence protection and unitizing sleeves. These sleeves largely serve the food and beverage, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical industries.

Khalid Khan, Founder and CEO of Ultrapak said, "By bringing this advanced production capacity directly to Chautauqua County, we are answering the call for stronger domestic supply chains. The successful installation of our printing press allows us to drastically reduce long lead times and vulnerabilities associated with offshore manufacturing. We are incredibly grateful to Empire State Development and our local partners for helping us scale our operations. This investment ensures that our customers nationwide can source premium, American-made flexible packaging with unparalleled speed, reliability, and precision."

Located at 134 Franklin Ave., Ultrapak has a long-trusted history serving national accounts, ranging from startups to established brands. Beyond shrink sleeves, Ultrapak also serves the flexible packaging market with flexible pouches and with sleeve application services.

"Chautauqua County has a proud manufacturing history, and investments like Ultrapak's demonstrate that our manufacturing sector continues to evolve and thrive,” Chautauqua County Executive PJ Wendel said. “This expansion represents a commitment to our local workforce, the creation of new job opportunities, and the long-term economic vitality of our communities. We are grateful to Ultrapak for its continued confidence in Chautauqua County and to our state and local partners for helping make this project possible."

entertainment.title: Bob Seger and the Silver Bullet Band Bassist Chris Campbell Dead at 78
entertainment.summary: He spent 50 years playing alongside Seger and appears on "Turn the Page," "Night Moves," "Rock and Roll Never Forgets," "Still the Same," "Hollywood Nights," and "Against the Wind"
entertainment.body:
Bob Seger and the Silver Bullet Band bassist Chris Campbell, who joined forces with Seger in 1969 and remained a core member of the band through Seger’s farewell tour in 2019 — playing on timeless hits like “Turn the Page,” “Night Moves,” “Rock and Roll Never Forgets,” “Still the Same,” “Hollywood Nights,” and “Against the Wind” — died on Sunday. He was 78.

Campbell’s wife, Courtney, confirmed his death with Rolling Stone , adding that Campbell died of natural causes.

“I’m grieving the loss of my long-time friend and Silver Bullet bandmate, Chris Campbell…..RIP,” Silver Bullet Band vocalist Shaun Murphy wrote. “Prayers and condolences to his wonderful wife, Courtney Campbell, and his three beautiful daughters!! I am forever grateful for all the cherished memories I have.”

Campbell grew up in Plymouth, Michigan, and was a regular on the Detroit club scene that gave rise to the MC5, the Stooges, and the Amboy Dukes. “You were playing to smaller crowds and things were more intimate,” he told the Observer & Eccentric in 1987. “There weren’t any barriers in front of the stage with six-foot security guards.”

Just one year after the Bob Seger System scored a nationwide hit with “Ramblin’ Gamblin’ Man” in 1968, Campbell was offered a spot in the band. “I was hired in what I thought was a temporary job as bass player because Dan Honaker had just broken his wrist about a week before the Mongrel tour [in a motorcycle accident],” he told Rolling Stone in 2011. “I had a week to prepare. I had to learn this album frontwards and backwards.”

Honaker’s bad luck turned out to be the opportunity of a lifetime for Campbell because of what transpired not long after the Bob Seger System dissolved. “Bob called me…I think it was ’71, ’72,” Campbell told Rolling Stone . “He said, ‘I’m thinking of putting a band together.’ I said to him, ‘That’s kind of bizarre, I have a keyboard player and a drummer.’ He goes, ‘I got a guitarist, Drew Abbott.’ That was the start of the Silver Bullet Band.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

The early years of the Silver Bullet Band were a brutal grind, memorialized in the lyrics of 1972’s “Turn the Page,” but everything changed once the concert LP Live Bullet took off in 1976. The follow-up LP, Night Moves , turned Seger into one of the biggest names in rock.

entertainment.title: Jessica Alba ordered by court to pay ex-husband Cash Warren whopping sum as part of their divorce
entertainment.summary: The actress and the producer split in 2024 after nearly 17 years of marriage.
entertainment.body:
Jessica Alba was ordered to pay ex-husband Cash Warren over half a million dollars as part of their divorce settlement.

The actress will have to pay the producer a staggering $577,481, according to court docs obtained by Page Six. The payout comes from Alba’s retirement benefits under her company HonorBar Inc’s Profit Sharing Plan.

The docs note that the amount will be adjusted for investment gains and losses through the date the funds are transferred.

After the payment, Alba won’t be required to pay her ex any additional benefits related to her company.

The judgment comes after Warren was given a $3 million payment to even out the distribution of assets when they settled their divorce in February. Alba was ordered to pay him in two $1.5 million payments, TMZ reported at the time.

The outlet also reported that the pair did not sign a prenuptial agreement despite Alba’s Honest Company being valued at $623 million and Warren’s sock and underwear brand, Pair of Thieves, being worth at least $100 million.

The exes share three children together — daughters Honor, 18, Haven, 15, and son Hayes, 8. The two share joint legal and physical custody of all of their kids.

They were married for 16 years before separating in December 2024.

entertainment.title: See the Sasha & Digweed Poster That Sold for $21,500 at Auction
entertainment.summary: The poster for the duo's 1994 mix album Renaissance: The Mix Collection was originally created as a temporary ad.
entertainment.body:
A recent auction of items related to Sasha & Digweed ‘s seminal 1996 mix album Northern Exposure included one lot that fetched far more than the rest.

“The reason is that most of these posters were stuck on billboard sites or in the tube station so they would not have been recoverable even when taken down,” Digweed tells Billboard on what made the poster so valuable. “I had kept a poster from that release and had forgot about it. When I was in my record room searching out the Northern Exposure vinyl, I remembered this poster was on the top shelf. It was in perfect condition and a real collectors piece from such a classic mix album release. In a world of scarcity this poster is very rare indeed. I can see why a massive fan would want it but was blown away by how much.”

Hosted by online auction platform Amplifyd, which has previously hosted auctions for items from artists including Danny Tenaglia, the Northern Exposure sale opened on Sept. 29 and closed Oct. 21. Featuring items from the producers’ personal archives, the auction included the actual records used to mix Northern Exposure , Northern Exposure 2, Northern Exposure: Expeditions and Communicate , in addition to various posters, flyers and other memorabilia.

All of the auction’s 113 lots brought winning bids, with the $21,500 poster being not only the highest-selling item of this auction, but the highest-selling item in Amplifyd history.

Sasha & Digweed have upcoming shows at The Roundhouse in London on Dec. 5 and EDC Mexico in February.

entertainment.title: New ‘Hunger Games’ Movie on the Way? Lionsgate Film Chief Shares Latest on Franchise’s Future
entertainment.summary: Adam Fogelson tells The Hollywood Reporter that his team hopes to connect soon with author Suzanne Collins about a new project: "I will sit patiently and wait for that phone call."
entertainment.body:
Logo text The Hunger Games franchise has whetted appetites for more films, given the success of its latest title.

Lionsgate released The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping over the weekend, with the movie grossing a commanding $119.3 million from 4,018 North American locations to open in first place at the box office . The feature adaptation of author Suzanne Collins ‘ 2025 prequel novel notched a better opening frame than the two most recent entries in the six-film series that kicked off with 2012’s Jennifer Lawrence -led The Hunger Games. Related Stories Movies 'You Can See Everything' Crosses $100M Globally, Becomes First Doc to Hit 1M Letterboxd Watches Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Slays $120M at Box Office as Franchise Heats Back Up

During a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter to celebrate the success of Sunrise on the Reaping , Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson emphasizes that the studio would love to collaborate again with Collins on another project in the franchise. Director Francis Lawrence ‘s latest movie stars Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, portrayed in the first four films by Woody Harrelson. The $150 million-budgeted feature is set 24 years before the events of Collins’ original 2008 book.

“We have complete respect for Suzanne as the architect,” Fogelson says. “I have told her that, if and when she is ready for me to read something else, I will drop everything and go anywhere in the world to get to read it. And I will sit patiently and wait for that phone call.”

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping had a far bigger impact at the box office than the 2023 prequel film The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , which starred Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer. Centering on the backstory for villainous President Snow — portrayed in the new movie by Ralph Fiennes — Songbirds and Snakes opened to $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million.

“All of us understood that the story that Suzanne wanted to tell on Songbirds was a challenging one and that she was inspired to tell it,” Fogelson explains. “She did it in an extraordinary way. Clearly, the movie worked really well for the audience that saw it, but the origin story of the villain — with no grand Hunger Games spectacle at the center of the story — is a challenging ask.”

entertainment.title: Robert Glasper on the State of R&B, Kendrick Lamar’s ‘To Pimp a Butterfly’ & Why ‘AI Can’t Copy This’
entertainment.summary: The five-time Grammy-winning musician also discusses jazz's influence on hip-hop, scoring upcoming films & helping shape the next generation of Blue Note Records.
entertainment.body:
Robert Glasper has spent his career challenging the boundaries of jazz , hip-hop, R&B and soul, bringing together sounds that don’t always share the same space. He’s the pianist behind some of the most important jazz and hip-hop collaborations of the last two decades. And as the music industry continues to evolve, the five-time Grammy-winning musician believes there’s still plenty of room for artists to explore beyond traditional genre boundaries.

In a conversation with Billboard , Glasper reflected on the changing musical landscape, the importance of originality, and why he believes the industry is becoming more open to artists embracing multiple influences.

“I feel like it’s catching up,” he says of the industry’s growing acceptance of genre blending. “We’re not all the way there, but I think that door is open to where people are more open to exploring different genres of music and artists not feeling like they have to be a monolithic thing.”

Glasper also shared his perspective on what separates a great musician from an artist who genuinely changes the direction of music, pointing to artists like Erykah Badu and Kendrick Lamar as examples of musicians who have shifted the culture.

“Those are people who have moved the needle,” he explains. “When they came around, they came with a different sound, a different outlook. It changed generations. It made generations want to be that.”

Robert then shifted gears to Lamar’s critically acclaimed 2015 album To Pimp a Butterfly , on which he worked. Glasper shared that he recorded his piano contributions to eight songs in less than an hour, as Lamar gave him the freedom to listen to each track and play whatever he felt was right. He had no idea the larger impact the album would eventually have.

In the full Billboard News interview, Glasper also discussed his upcoming film-scoring projects, including Miles and Juliet and Don’t Ever Wonder 2 , and his take on AI, and why he isn’t worried about what the technology means for his craft.

“AI can’t make mistakes, and I think that’s what makes humans human,” he says. “The imperfection is what makes humans human, and the imperfections are the things I feel are the sweet spots in music in general.”

entertainment.title: Jagged Edge Member Brandon Casey Sued by Woman Claiming Child Rape
entertainment.summary: The woman also alleges she wrote the R&B group’s hit song “Walked Outta Heaven” at age six. Casey "flatly rejects the untrue allegations."
entertainment.body:
Brandon Casey of the R&B group Jagged Edge is facing a lawsuit that claims he sexually assaulted a young girl over the course of several years in the early 2000s.

Casey was sued in September by a 29-year-old woman named Tyliyah Lee, who alleges she was repeatedly raped by the singer after meeting him at a Philadelphia “community event” in 2003. Casey’s lawyer, Leron Rogers of the firm Fox Rothschild, said in a Monday (Nov. 23) statement to Billboard that the singer “flatly rejects the untrue allegations of battery and sexual assault set forth in the civil complaint.”

“The claims stem from events alleged to have occurred some twenty years ago, are baseless and unsupported by any corroboration we are aware of and have already been met with a firm denial in court,” added Rogers.

The lawsuit, obtained by Billboard , alleges that Casey had nonconsensual sexual intercourse with Lee on five separate occasions when she was between six and 10 years old. Lee is now suing Casey for battery and seeking at least $50,000 in damages for “severe emotional distress and substantial depression and anxiety.” Lee, who is a singer-songwriter, also claims in the lawsuit that she wrote the 2003 Jagged Edge hit “Walked Outta Heaven” when she was just six years old. She says Casey stole the song from her after she played it for him and never compensated her. “Walked Outta Heaven” hit No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on Billboard ‘s Hot R&B/Hip Hop Songs chart.

Lee initially brought the lawsuit in a Philadelphia county court in September. On Thursday (Nov. 19), Casey’s attorneys moved the case to federal court. That court filing says Casey “denies each and every allegation of wrongdoing in the complaint” and notes that before she sued, Lee demanded a $15 million settlement from the singer.

“Mr. Casey will not be pressured by headlines, and he will not stand by while his name and reputation are attacked,” Rogers said in his Monday statement to Billboard . “We intend to pursue sanctions and every other available remedy against the Plaintiff and her counsel for bringing claims we believe have no basis in fact. Mr. Casey believes genuine survivors of abuse deserve a voice and our full respect, and baseless claims only diminish their cause.”

entertainment.title: Jay-Z’s 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show Coming to IMAX Theaters
entertainment.summary: Get your popcorn ready.
entertainment.body:
“This ain’t a movie, dog,” Jay-Z says on “Public Service Announcement (Interlude)” — but this time around, it is.

The NFL, Disney and ESPN collectively announced on Monday (Nov. 23) that Hov’s Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show will be getting the IMAX treatment.

With the Super Bowl broadcasting on ESPN for the first time in its history, the big game is set to air in IMAX theaters across the U.S. and select international markets.

According to Variety , tickets will go on sale in January, with Super Bowl LXI slated for Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.

Theaters hosting the Super Bowl in IMAX will also be announced in the coming weeks. There will be a four-hour presentation of the game’s entirety, including Hov’s halftime show, as well as a pre and post-game show.

“Watching the Super Bowl with your fellow fans is one of the great shared experiences in sports, and this first-of-its-kind collaboration with the NFL and IMAX takes it to a historic new scale,” said Ken Potrock, who serves as the Walt Disney Company’s president of major event integration, per Variety. “With ESPN’s first Super Bowl, we’re reaching fans across an unprecedented range of platforms and meeting them wherever they want to be, with unique moments that only Disney and ESPN can deliver.”

Jay-Z was announced as the 2027 Super Bowl headliner during a Monday Night Football broadcast on Oct. 26, just days after he performed a pair of concerts at SoFi Stadium.

The Brooklyn rap deity has been back outside this year. He returned to the stage in May at Roots Picnic and hosted a blockbuster three-night stay at Yankee Stadium in July, before heading across the pond for dates in London and Paris.

entertainment.title: 5 Ways HBO's Harry Potter Series Could Improve On The Original Quidditch Scenes
entertainment.summary: Quidditch, the quintessential game of Harry Potter, is one thing fans are asking for more of in the upcoming TV series. Here's how HBO can make it work.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Harry Potter" fans haven't seen a proper on-screen Quidditch match since 2009, which has been far too long. Sure, Quidditch wouldn't make sense as a real game — the mere fact that any match could technically end within the first two minutes (or go on for weeks) would drive both the players and the spectators crazy — but that's irrelevant. Quidditch is perfectly designed to let Harry (now played by Dominic McLaughlin) be the hero of every game.

Quidditch also adds some extra texture to the wizarding world, provides a fun break from the doom and gloom of whatever scheme Voldemort's pulling, and it's used to add some extra stakes to Harry's social life. Harry's relationship to his school bully Draco, to his crush Cho Chang, and to his friend Ron Weasley are all complicated by Quidditch.

That's why it's a shame that the movies never emphasized the sport that much. Among the many mistakes the movies made , the treatment of Quidditch is one of the biggest the upcoming show could address. If the TV show wants to do justice to this delightfully nonsensical game, here are five things it can do differently from the films.

HBO It's established early on in the books that Hogwarts' Quidditch games aren't just about bragging rights between the Houses. When a House's team wins a game, they win a lot of points towards their House Cup score. This is particularly important in the first novel, as Gryffindor's two Quidditch wins prove instrumental in allowing them to come from behind and take the House championship from Slytherin.

The movies, however, don't establish the connection between the House points and the Quidditch matches. As far as movie-only viewers are concerned, the House Cup comes down entirely to students' behavior and nothing else. While that would probably be the more reasonable system for the school, the system established in the books helps to link the Quidditch subplot with the House Cup subplot, heightening the stakes of the games; including this detail should be a no-brainer for the series.

Warner Bros/HBO Max One of the biggest fan complaints about the movie adaptation of "Goblet of Fire" is the treatment of the Quidditch World Cup. The movie dedicates so much time to the characters arriving at the cup and settling in for the game, but skips over the event itself.

The reasons for this are obvious: the book this film's adapting is the longest (and arguably most convoluted) in the series. The movie had to make tough decisions, and the World Cup is technically not that important to the main plot. (The fourth film is also infamous among Potterheads for cutting the most characters from its source material .) The TV show, however, should have more than enough time to do both the main story and the World Cup justice.

entertainment.title: DIG Video: Amy Poehler Explains Why Her Character Is The Anti-Leslie Knope — Plus, Grade The Series!
entertainment.summary: Amy Poehler tells us why her DIG character Elise is the complete opposite of Leslie Knope from Parks and Rec - plus, give the series a grade in our poll.
entertainment.body:
Amy Poehler is teaming up again with "Parks and Recreation" co-creator Michael Schur for their new Peacock comedy "DIG" ... but don't expect her character to give any inspiring, uplifting speeches.

In "DIG," Poehler's character Elise is cranky, cynical, and not exactly a people person. She bristles both at her older boss Neville, played by Hugh Laurie, and her Gen Z underlings. She's not nearly as upbeat as Leslie Knope, the character Poehler played on "Parks and Rec"... but as Poehler tells TVLine in the video above: "Neither am I! Very few people are."

To Poehler, Elise represents Generation X, "my generation," and "they're quite disaffected. They are really often kind of checked out, and they have raised themselves. So they remember how things used to be." They're stuck in the middle, generation-wise, she adds: "Boomers have been their bosses," and "the young women that come [after] them have completely different experiences and opportunities."

She does admit that Elise is "prickly, kind of grouchy, and not especially good with people." But she enjoyed that "for the first time ever, [I] got to play somebody who wasn't worried about taking care of other people... which is, I guess, what it's like being a man in the world!"

entertainment.title: Bela Bajaria Calls Time at Netflix a “Fun Chapter” as She Teases Rest and “Conversations” in First Remarks on Exit
entertainment.summary: The former chief content officer at the streaming service was ousted last month, with Peter Rice taking over her role.
entertainment.body:
Former Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria addressed her exit from the streamer in her first public comments about her abrupt departure last month.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter ahead of the 2026 International Emmys , where she’s set to be honored with the Founders Award , Bajaria called her decade at Netflix “such an amazing, fun chapter” and shared she was “proud of so many of the things” that she and her team had accomplished.

Since her exit, Bajaria said she’s been indulging in “a little rest” and having some “really fun conversations.” Related Stories Movies Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie 'Malibu' From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive) Movies 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-The-Line Shortlists

“I’m excited about what’s next, and I think this time is good for a little rest after a lot of global travel,” she told THR on the red carpet ahead of the awards show, adding that she’s “really open” to whatever the future holds.

Bajaria was ousted from her role at Netflix on Oct. 15, with former Fox and Disney exec Peter Rice taking her place as chief content officer.

The former chief content officer previously spoke with THR at the Saban Community Clinic Gala at the end of October but wasn’t yet ready to speak about her time at Netflix. Still she offered, “the outpouring that I’ve received in the last couple of weeks has been so beautiful and amazing. I’ve been in television for 30 years, and at this point I have worked with what feels like nearly every single person from agents and producers to writers and actors. I love it. I’m so grateful for the career I have had to date, with lots more to come.”

Speaking to THR at the International Emmys, Bajaria also weighed in on the recent departures of a number of top female executives amid ongoing layoffs and restructuring efforts, including Pam Abdy at Warner Bros. and Cindy Holland at Paramount.

“I think in general, in every industry, we just have to make sure that you have leaders that are doing a great job and really care about the group and are making those decisions,” Bajaria said. “And it matters who’s in those roles, and I think we should always just be aware of that.”

entertainment.title: ‘GTA 6’ Boss Strauss Zelnick Among First Raft of SXSW London 2027 Speakers
entertainment.summary: The upcoming installment — built around the theme "The Power of Human Potential" — has also enlisted former DeepMind creative lead Jon Steinback and president of Genomics Limited David Thornton.
entertainment.body:
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick, the man behind Grand Theft Auto VI , is among the first raft of speakers confirmed for next year’s SXSW London .

The conference is set to return to Shoreditch, east London, for its third year from May 24-29, where Zelnick will take to the stage to talk about building one of the world’s biggest entertainment franchises (sales for the latest release have already out-grossed Christopher Nolan’s box office behemoth The Odyssey ).

The upcoming installment is built around the theme “The Power of Human Potential,” described by organizers as a deliberate focus on people in a year dominated by what machines can do. Among the speakers making that case is Jon Steinback, the former DeepMind creative lead whose start-up Marker is building an AI writing tool designed to develop, rather than delete, writers. Related Stories Movies How Iran's Pegah Ahangarani Turned Her Family Archives Into a Regime-Challenging Oscar Hopeful Music Don Toliver Postpones O2 Arena Show After Evacuation Due to "Unknown Substance" Released at Manchester Concert

Elsewhere, David Thornton, president of Genomics Limited, will explore how rapid analysis of large-scale genetic and genomic information will empower us to predict disease risks and improve medicine.

Ilyas Khan, who founded Cambridge Quantum and was the founding CEO of Quantinuum, is also on board to discuss the convergence of AI and quantum computing. His appearance follows Quantinuum’s $1.68bn Nasdaq listing in June 2026, the largest traditional IPO yet for a pure-play quantum computing company.

The event will welcome around 20,000 festival-goers on its walkable Shoreditch campus, engaging in networking, music showcases, international premieres and parties. The 2026 festival drew attendees from 97 countries, 863 speakers (including Michelle Obama, Serena Williams and Brian Eno), 256 music artists across 18 venues and 100 film screenings, 13 of them world premieres.

“I hated that,” Rogen confessed on the Nov. 16 episode of the Happy Sad Confused podcast. “That was not fun.”

The 44-year-old explained that he was convinced to appear on the season six episode “Rock Bottom” by his former Freaks and Geeks costar and Dawson’s Creek actress Busy Philipps after she appeared on his show Undeclared .

“She was like, ‘Hey, now that I’m doing this, you gotta do Dawson’s Creek .’ And I was like, ‘Haha,’” Rogen recalled. “And then, like, six months later, I’m on the set of Dawson’s Creek. I was like, ‘How did this happen?’”

And according to the Emmy winner, the drama wasn’t just onscreen, as he revealed there was plenty behind-the-scenes, too.

“It was so weird,” he shared. “And there was a lot of resentment between, like, the showrunners and the cast—it was a very bad dynamic.”

He had quite a harrowing experience away from the set, too, adding, “I was staying in, like, a haunted hotel and had a nervous breakdown.”

E! News has reached out to Dawson’s Creek creator Kevin Williamson , as well as showrunners Greg Berlanti and Tom Kapinos for comment but has not heard back.

In our book, we need a little alpine charm in our life every single day this winter. How else could we keep ourselves from freezing during the coldest temperatures?

Fair Isle sweaters are a traditional knitting style that features a distinctive pattern with multiple colors —either bold or neutral shades. The most trendy pattern we're seeing right now is geometric styles around the neckline or the center of the sweater. Still, even though it's adorable and cozy, this type of sweater might seem difficult to style.

Luckily, we've got you covered. No need to freeze in front of your closet when getting dressed in the morning! And the best part? Carve Designs has the chic Fair Isle sweaters and the styles to pair it with on sale for 25% off , just in time for Black Friday .

So, keep scrolling to see how we'd recommend pairing this (apparently) controversial and traditional sweater.

1. The most popular way to style the Fair Isle sweaters is with jeans. It's a no-brainer. You can style it more casually with relaxed boyfriend jeans or light-wash barrel jeans , paired with boots or sneakers. It can also feel dressier with a dark wide-leg jean , styled with gold jewelry, heels, and a chic shoulder bag—while keeping that cozy comfort with the trendy pattern.

2. If you want to make your outfit a little more interesting (but still casual), the Fair Isle sweater can also be styled with this pair of corduroy pants . We recommend opting for a maxi skirt and pairing it with knee-high boots—either a silky one in a light color or a dark-wash denim one .
