entertainment.title: ‘Do You Have What It Takes?’: KATSEYE Appears in Trailer for K-Pop Film Inspired by Their Experience
entertainment.summary: K-Pop: The Debut follows a televised competition series aiming to form the next global girl group.
entertainment.body:
The upcoming movie K-Pop: The Debut centers on a televised competition series aiming to assemble a “truly global girl group” with contestants from all over the world. Sound familiar? It definitely does to KATSEYE .

That’s why it only makes sense that the real-life girl group makes a cameo in the film, as shown in a new trailer that dropped Monday (Nov. 23). “Hey, it’s KATSEYE!” members Daniela, Sophia, Megan, Lara and Yoonchae say in unison at the beginning of the preview, after which Yoonchae asks: “Do you have what it takes to debut as the next K-pop superstar?”

The trailer then introduces viewers to leading lady Lizzy Lee — played by Ji-young Yoo — who is working toward becoming a doctor but dreams of being a star. After seeing KATSEYE’s callout, she sends in an audition tape for K-Pop Superstar , which leads her to travel to Korea to compete amongst dozens of other hopefuls with varying levels of dance skills, vocal abilities and humility.

“We want to create a truly global girl group with the best talent in the world,” an executive says at one point in the trailer over scenes of Lee and her competitors in intense rehearsals and performing together on stage.

Arriving in theaters on Feb. 26 next year, the Benson Lee-directed project will feature a star-studded soundtrack of songs by BTS, aespa, ENHYPEN, Twice, JISOO of BLACKPINK and, of course, KATSEYE. It’ll also star Eric Nam, Jitae Yoo, Tony Revolori, Gia Kim, Yim Si-wan, Ahin Lee, Aliyah Turner, Renata Vaca, Sung Jun, Kang Sora, Hyongchol Lee, Silia Kapsis, Shana Kim and Park Jubi.

“A young Korean-American woman has spent her life following the path her family chose for her,” a synopsis reads. “But when she earns a spot in a globally televised competition to form the next K-pop girl group, she travels to Seoul, South Korea, to pursue the dream she must still keep hidden. Surrounded by extraordinary performers from around the world, all competing for just four coveted spots, Lizzy must push herself further than she ever imagined.”

The Paramount Pictures film was produced in part by Hybe Americas, three years after Hybe x Geffen’s The Debut: Dream Academy experiment. The K-Pop: The Debut trailer does not directly cite KATSEYE’s experience as inspiration, but its plot does follow the Dream Academy premise to a tee; just like in the movie, the 2023 web series narrowed down a class of trainees through a combination of judge and fan voting to determine who would earn a spot in what the company billed as the world’s first global girl group .

entertainment.title: Mary J. Blige’s ‘Real Love’ Did Not Infringe on ‘Impeach the President,’ Appeals Court Rules
entertainment.summary: “The works as a whole are distinct,” the three-judge panel found
entertainment.body:
In a 10-page ruling from the Second Circuit Court of Appeals, the justices found that the 2024 lawsuit filed by Tuff City Records against Universal Music Publishing failed to state a viable claim. The ruling found that the two songs “are not substantially similar as a matter of law.”

“The works as a whole are distinct,” the ruling obtained by Rolling Stone reads. “The songs differ in their lyrics, melody, genre, subject matter, and overall sound.”

The Honey Drippers released “Impeach the President” in 1973, and it quickly became a Nixon-era protest anthem with a distinctive drum break that would become widely sampled by artists including Janet Jackson, J. Cole, and Doja Cat.

In filing its appeal, Tuff City argued that the lower court used an incorrect legal standard to compare “Real Love” with “Impeach the President.” The appellate court disagreed.

“While ‘Impeach the President’ and ‘Real Love’ share certain percussive elements, other elements are notably different, such as open versus closed hi-hats and distinct snare and kick drum rhythms,” the ruling states. “The songs’ ‘total concept and overall feel’ reinforce the conclusion that the works at issue are not substantially similar.”

Agreeing with the district court, the ruling found that “Impeach the President” is a protest song that “fits squarely within the soul/funk genre,” whereas “Real Love” is a “hip-hop soul song about heartbreak, not politics.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

entertainment.title: Why Dick York's Darrin Stephens Left Bewitched After 5 Seasons
entertainment.summary: Dick York's sudden departure from "Bewitched" and its recasting of the character Darrin left many wondering what caused the actor's departure from the show.
entertainment.body:

The departure of Dick York's Darrin Stephens from "Bewitched" is a particularly tragic instance of an actor leaving a role because their health couldn't keep up. In the 2024 "Bewitched 60th: Anniversary Special" documentary, Sandra Gould (who was the second actor to play Gladys Kravitz) discussed York's dependency on medication due to an injury he had suffered: "He was on all kinds of pain pills. And it finally got so bad that he just couldn't work anymore, and it was devastating ... But you could just see the pain in his eyes."

Dick York's health concerns began when he was filming the Western "They Came to Cordura" in 1959. York recounted the injury. When he was propelling a suspended handcar carrying wounded soldiers, an extra pulled the handle that York was operating, and York was suddenly forced to bear the brunt of a human's weight: "Now, instead of lifting the expected weight, I was suddenly, jarringly, lifting his entire weight off the flatbed—180 pounds or so. The muscles along the right side of my back tore. They just snapped and let loose" (via Biography ). His back injury continued to deteriorate until he collapsed on the "Bewitched" set in February 1969 and suffered a seizure while unconscious, a day York described as "the worst day of my life" in the anniversary special.

ABC Despite his injury, York continued working through the pain, appearing in two episodes of "The Twilight Zone" and in episodes of "Alfred Hitchcock Presents." During his time on "Bewitched," filming was adjusted to accommodate York's health. His character's activities were limited because he was incapacitated; a slanted wall was built for him to lean on because he couldn't stand for too long, and lots of makeup was applied to him because he looked too ill. At the time of his departure, York's explanation for exiting "Bewitched" was that he wanted "the chance to do other stage and movie roles" (via Biography).

York's first appearance on "Bewitched" was the series premiere, "I, Darrin, Take This Witch, Samantha," and he played the husband of Samantha Stephens (Elizabeth Montgomery). The last episode he appeared in was "Samantha and Darrin in Mexico City," the Season 5 finale. Rather than writing out the character, the role of Darrin Stephens was recast , and Dick Sargent began playing the character from Season 6.

entertainment.body:
On Monday morning, CNBC senior Washington correspondent Eamon Javers was driving in his car when the President of the United States called.

Javers pulled over to the side of the road, and within minutes he and President Trump were live on Squawk on the Street to talk about Nvidia ‘s shock decision to bring back CEO Jensen Huang. Trump was on the show for nearly an hour, revealing his central role in securing Huang’s return.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter Monday afternoon, KC Sullivan, the president of CNBC, called this morning’s coverage of Huang and Nvidia a “really special moment.”

“The President was so generous with his time, but it was fun to see Eamon bring that in, and then to have [Jim] Cramer jump in, Sara Eisen jump in, Carl Quintanilla jump in, David Faber jump in, and to be able to get all those different perspectives, I just think it made such a rich discussion,” Sullivan said. “I was really just so proud of the team and how they delivered.”

For months, the news business has been focused on the 2026 midterm elections, and for good reason. But the midterms are over, and suddenly it seems the most consequential stories of this moment in time are happening on CNBC.

Nvidia stock soared 31.8 percent on Monday after the news, and the entire stock market rallied. Huang and Nvidia are not only a business story, they are an economic story, a political story, a national security story. It’s a story of our time. For CNBC, it was also the second highest hour of web traffic this year, behind only SpaceX’s IPO in June.

“In the world of media now, it’s those who are essential to their audience and really understand their brand promise and deliver on that are the ones that are going to going to thrive,” Sullivan says. “I do think that there’s a lot of attention on the business world right now, and I don’t think there’s anybody who can compete with us in that arena.”

For CNBC, that audience includes Trump, as well as seemingly every CEO of note in America. “I want to congratulate you guys. You covered it really well,” Trump told the Squawk on the Street hosts during his marathon interview.

entertainment.title: Burning Man CEO Marian Goodell to Exit: ‘I’m Not Tired, I’m Not Done — I’m Ready to Be a Mentor’
entertainment.summary: Burning Man’s CEO since 2013, Goodell will remain in the role during the search for a new leader and keep her seat on the Burning Man board.
entertainment.body:
Burning Man Project’s longtime CEO Marian Goodell has announced that she’s leaving the position.

Goodell will remain as CEO during the search for a new leader of Burning Man Project, the nonprofit organization behind the annual gathering in Nevada’s Black Rock Desert that also supports the global Burning Man community, including the worldwide network of official Regional Burning Man Events . Goodell will remain on the Burning Man board after stepping down.

Goodell tells Billboard that while there is no set goal date to have someone new in the CEO role, she’s “fairly confident that having somebody in place at the beginning of the year — so they can spend some time with me — is a reasonable expectation.” She says that as one of the co-founders of Burning Man, she’s keen to help mentor a new CEO who will serve as the next generation of leadership in the event’s four-decade history.

Burning Man has hired a search firm to assist with finding a new CEO, with the organization anticipating that it will field candidates from the global Burning Man community and beyond. Anyone can put themselves or someone else forward for the role at executivesearch@burningman.org .

Goodell first went to Burning Man in 1995 — the sixth year the gathering happened in the Black Rock Desert after its early years on San Francisco’s Baker Beach. She helped found the Burning Man Project organization in 1997 and has been CEO since 2013. The organization now has 130 full-time employees.

Goodell shepherded Burning Man through an acutely challenging era. Burning Man co-founder Larry Harvey died in 2018 , and the Black Rock City event was canceled in 2020 and 2021 due to the pandemic. This gathering subsequently experienced several difficult years due to weather, most notably a rain event in 2023, along with funding challenges that led the organization to launch a $20 million fundraising push in 2024.

Goodell says that as she exits the role, the next CEO “is inheriting a company and an organization that’s financially stable, that is behaving very responsibly about managing costs.” She notes that attendance at Black Rock City 2026 was roughly 64,000, a number the organization plans on capping going forward.

“If we look at what’s happening around the world and the culture, it doesn’t make sense to keep pretending that we could be at 78,000 [attendees] while gas prices are what they are, and Canadians don’t want to come to America,” says Goodell. “We need to be able to plan for expenses, size, volunteers, leadership, ice sales, etc. Why not just cap it at a place we found really amazing this year?”

sports.title: Report: NFL Primetime documentary is in the works
sports.summary: The recent passing of Tom Jackson has sparked much discussion about ESPN's NFL Primetime, which was for years a mandatory Sunday evening destination for football fans everywhere.
sports.body:
As it turns out, a documentary is coming regarding the show.

Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing , the final product is believed to be on track for a release in connection with the Super Bowl, which is being televised by ESPN and ABC.

It could be part of the game-day programming. Three years ago, CBS debuted You Are Looking Live! — a documentary about The NFL Today — before the launch of the official pregame show in advance of Super Bowl LVIII.

For those who were actively following the NFL in the late ‘80s, NFL Primetime provided the first opportunity to see extended highlights of NFL games on the day they were played. Years before the Internet, social media, Sunday Ticket, and RedZone, Primetime became appointment viewing for fans who wanted to see more about what was happening beyond the two or three games available in their local markets on Sunday afternoon.

And the team of Chris Berman and Tom Jackson became the tour guides for the opportunity to essentially watch all of the important plays from every game in a compressed but meaningful package, with Berman’s cadence and the music accompanying the words creating the loose impression that it was all happening live. Even though everyone knew it wasn’t.

It became a unique moment in time, which at the time didn’t seem to have a shelf life. It’s just the way things were, with fans having no concept that there would ever be a way to watch all of the games live or to see any and all relevant plays long before 7:00 p.m. ET. It was a new frontier that no one had reason to believe would not remain a permanent fixture of each and every NFL Sunday.

As Neumann explains it, Jackson recently made a surprise return to ESPN as part of the filming of the documentary. ESPN shared footage of the reunion on Sunday.

It’s worth your time to watch it, if you were one of the millions who climbed aboard the Primetime Express every Sunday night of football season for something much more meaningful than a glimpse of the entire day of NFL action. And the documentary will undoubtedly bring back fond memories of the final years before advances in technology caused a narrow range of football options to explode into today’s endless menu of choices.

sports.title: Bears have gone five straight games without ever trailing for first time since 1985
sports.summary: The Bears' win over the Saints on Sunday was their fifth consecutive game taking a first-quarter lead and winning without ever trailing.
sports.body:
The last Bears team to win five straight games without ever trailing was the 1985 Bears, one of the most dominant teams in NFL history.

That 1985 Bears team lost just one game, a Monday night classic against the Dolphins in the 13th game of the season, and after that loss to the Dolphins they never trailed in the final three games of the regular season, or in the two playoff games they won to earn a trip to Super Bowl XX. In the Super Bowl, the Bears fell behind 3-0 in the first quarter before winning 46-10, snapping their streak of five straight games without trailing.

This Bears team isn’t dominating quite like that 1985 team, but the Bears are currently on a very impressive run: They haven’t just won five games in a row, but they’ve scored in every quarter of all five games, the franchise’s first streak of 20 consecutive quarters scoring since the 1941 Bears. That team, like the 1985 team, won the NFL championship.

The 2026 Bears are playing like some of the best teams in franchise history. They’re jumping out to early leads and never looking back.

Still, 12.23 million watched the game between the Colts and Texans, on average. It was the smallest Thursday night audience of the season, and it represented a nine-percent drop from last year’s Week 11 Thursday night game between the Jets and Patriots.

The game also faced competition from the release of the new Grand Theft Auto video game.

The latest game dragged the full-season average under 17 million for the first time this year. It now stands at 16.62 million per game.

sports.title: Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs listed as limited in practice again on Monday
sports.summary: The Packers' injury report for Monday looks a lot like the one they turned in on Sunday.
sports.body:
Defensive end Micah Parsons (knee) and running back Josh Jacobs (finger) remained limited participants. Parsons is expected to make his 2026 debut on Wednesday night against the Rams and Jacobs is trying to return after missing the Packers’ last game in Week 10.

Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), offensive lineman Travis Glover (shoulder), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), wide receiver Bo Melton (thigh), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) were limited participants. Glover was the only new addition to that group on Monday.

Cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib) moved from limited to full participation while guard Aaron Banks (knee) remained in that category.

sports.title: Rams upgrade RB Kyren Williams to full participant on Monday's injury report
sports.summary: While any injury news about the Rams has largely been bad this season, there was a positive development on the team's Monday practice report.
sports.body:
Running back Kyren Williams (toe) was upgraded from a limited to a full participant in the day’s session.

Williams With how many skill players are unavailable, Williams presence is critical for both the run and pass game. He leads the team with 616 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns. He also has 38 catches for 267 yards with a TD in 2026.

Safety Kam Curl (toe) was also upgraded from a non-participant on Sunday to limited on Monday.

Offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), offensive lineman Coleman Shelton (hamstring), and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not participate, with Ferguson set to stay on injured reserve for the rest of the season as he undergoes ankle surgery.

Defensive end Aaron Donald, outside linebacker Myles Garrett, tight end Tyler Higbee, and outside linebacker Byron Young all received a rest day.

Tight end Davis Allen (oblique), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), offensive lineman Justin Dedich (hand), linebacker Nate Landman (toe), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), defensive end Kobie Turner (groin), and quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) were al full participants.

sports.title: Marlon Humphrey back with Ravens, Jesse Minter doesn't commit to Week 12 return to lineup
sports.summary: Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was back at the team's facility on Monday.
sports.body:
The Ravens sent Humphrey home last week and deactivated him for Sunday’s loss to the Panthers after Humphrey made derogatory comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Humphrey apologized, but Minter said the decision to sit him out last week was made after conversations inside the organization.

Minter did not divulge details of that conversation and declined to share any of what he and Humphrey talked about on Monday. He said a decision on Humphrey’s return against the Texans in Week 12 will be made later in the week.

“I expect us to work through the week and see where we’re at,” Minter said.

Humphrey started the first 10 games of the season and has 40 tackles, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery this year.

sports.title: Bengals activate LB Swayze Bozeman, G Brian Parker from injured reserve
sports.summary: The Bengals announced a pair of roster moves on Monday afternoon.
sports.body:
Linebacker Swayze Bozeman and guard Brian Parker have both been activated from injured reserve. They will both be available to play against the Commanders in Monday night’s game in Washington.

Bozeman was claimed off of waivers during the offseason and he appeared in four games before going on injured reserve with a forearm injury. He had four tackles while playing a regular role on special teams in those contests.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and he was placed on injured reserve at the end of August. Parker has been dealing with a knee injury.

sports.title: DK Metcalf will not be suspended for actions during Steelers-Eagles
sports.summary: According to multiple reports, while Metcalf has avoided a suspension, he may still be fined.
sports.body:
Metcalf was ejected for committing two unsportsmanlike conduct fouls over the course of the game.

Metcalf then left the locker room without speaking to reporters. But spoke to them on Monday, denying the accusation that he was trying to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye.

It’s been a trying year for Metcalf, who has just 36 catches for 434 yards with two touchdowns in 10 games. That the receiver will not be suspended is a positive development for him. But Pittsburgh would surely like to see Metcalf increase his production and reduce the on-field antics that do not help the team.

sports.title: Commanders activate Jacory Croskey-Merritt
sports.summary: The Commanders have made an addition to their offensive backfield ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.
sports.body:
Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was activated from injured reserve on Monday afternoon. The Commanders released cornerback Isaac Yiadom in a corresponding move.

Croskey-Merritt was a full participant in practice this week and he was listed as questionable on Washington’s final injury report. He has missed the last four games with a groin injury.

Croskey-Merritt had 67 carries for 239 yards and two touchdowns in five games before his injury.

The Commanders listed Rachaad White as questionable with a heel injury that kept him out of practice Saturday. Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry are the other backs on the active roster for Washington.

sports.title: Giants CB Greg Newsome out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
sports.summary: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.
sports.body:
Head coach John Harbaugh said at his Monday press conference that Newsome suffered a high-ankle sprain. Harbaugh said that Newsome will be out multiple weeks as a result of the injury.

Newsome only played four snaps before being forced out of Sunday’s game. He has 35 tackles, an interception and eight passes defensed in his nine appearances this season.

That play earned Newsome a three-year extension beyond the one-year deal he signed with the team in the offseason, but the Giants will have to turn elsewhere in the secondary for the near future.

sports.title: Vikings "don't necessarily expect" Jordan Addison back this week
sports.summary: The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.
sports.body:
Addison has missed the last two games with a thumb injury that required surgery, but O’Connell said last week that the outlook was “really encouraging” for Addison’s return. The Vikings opted not to put him on injured reserve, which points to a return before missing four games but O’Connell didn’t make it sound like that would happen against the Falcons this week.

“Encouraged a bout where Jordan’s at,” O’Connell said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. “Don’t necessarily expect to have him this week but he’s progressing really well for having just gotten that thing fixed.”

The Vikings will host the Panthers in Week 13 and O’Connell’s next update on Addison’s progress may not come until closer to that matchup.

sports.title: Cardinals fire defensive coordinator Nick Rallis
sports.summary: Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator.
sports.body:
The Cardinals have fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

Rallis, 33, was retained under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur after previously serving in the same role under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Rallis came with Gannon from Philadelphia, where Gannon had served as defensive coordinator and Rallis was linebackers coach.

The Cardinals have struggled mightily on defense this season, with the unit currently ranked No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 31 in points allowed. The team had offered little resistance in losses to the Rams and Chiefs in consecutive weeks, with both teams scoring 34 points.

Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will serve as interim defensive coordinator. He was Pittsburgh’s DC under Mike Tomlin from 2022 to 2025. He previously served as defensive coordinator for the Lions and Bengals.

sports.title: Super Bowl LXI will be shown in IMAX theaters
sports.summary: The Super Bowl will be shown on some very big screens this season.
sports.body:
ESPN’s broadcast of Super Bowl LXI will be shown live in IMAX theaters as part of an agreement among the NFL, Disney and IMAX.

The game will air live in IMAX theaters in the U.S., Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. The show will include the game itself, the halftime show, pregame and postgame.

IMAX has grown increasingly popular for its huge, curved screens and immersive sound. The format is known for movies like The Odyssey , not for live sports, but the opportunity to watch the Super Bowl on the biggest screen in town will draw plenty of fans who will be curious to see what the game looks like on a screen so big that the players are larger than life.

sports.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson to undergo season-ending ankle surgery
sports.summary: One of the Rams' young pass-catchers will not be able to return in 2026.
sports.body:
Via multiple reporters, head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

Ferguson was on track to return earlier this month before suffering a hamstring injury at practice.

But now his ankle has not responded to treatment the way he or the team anticipated.

“ Didn’t necessarily feel great , but he had a really good week of practice but you could still see he was kind of getting comfortable,” McVay said of the process with Ferguson, via Adam Grosbard of the Southern California News Group. “Took some meds to be able to do that. Gets the hamstring on a Friday, and then, as he’s really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it, and it was like something in his deltoid and his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want.

“I don’t know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it’s just not coming along, and he wouldn’t be able to be himself and put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete, some of the change of direction, moving him across the formation.”

Ferguson is now set to remain on injured reserve for the rest of the year.

A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Ferguson was able to appear in just three games this year, catching seven passes for 63 yards with a touchdown. He caught 11 passes for 231 yards with three TDs in 14 games as a rookie last year.

sports.title: Shane Steichen says Colts have not shut down Alec Pierce for the season
sports.summary: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.
sports.body:
Pierce has not played since aggravating a heel injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2 and the Colts’ recent roster moves have made it clear that they have shifted their attention to the 2027 season. While that may be the case, head coach Shane Steichen said on Monday that the team has not made any call about whether Pierce will return in their final six games.

“I know there’s reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season,” Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. “We have not made that determination. He’s still going through his rehab process. The only way we’ll put him out there is if he’s 100 percent. We gotta be really smart.”

Pierce has a short window to get to 100 percent before the season is over and bringing him back from a long layoff may not be the best way to ensure that he’s at full strength for next season, so it may just be a matter of when rather than if the Colts ultimately decide to shut the wideout down until next year.

sports.title: Terrion Arnold's lawyer seeks sanctions for discovery violation
sports.summary: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave with eight felony charges pending in Florida.
sports.body:
On Monday, attorney Harvey Steinberg filed a motion for sanctions, arising from the alleged failure of the prosecution to timely disclose as discovery material.

The gist of the 13-page filing is that the prosecution withheld a statement from defendant Boakai Hilton until after another defendant, Arianna Del Valle, sat for a sworn, pre-trial deposition.

Hilton’s statement, per the filing, conflicts with statements made by Del Valle. By not having the Hilton statement, Steinberg was unable to properly question Del Valle about the discrepancies.

On the surface, it’s an easy fix. Steinberg should get another chance to question Del Valle under oath. At a deeper level, the situation (if it unfolded the way Steinberg alleges) speaks to the integrity of the process.

Prosecutors have immense power and discretion, which should be exercised at all times with the goal of doing justice. Sometimes, a blind desire to “win” can overcome the mandate to do justice, thereby corrupting the system.

The Hillsborough County prosecutor’s office is already dealing with an unrelated case in which “winning” may have trumped justice. A prosecutor recently resigned for failing to disclose during jury selection that the sister of a fellow prosecutor was in the jury pool for a rape trial. The woman ultimately served as the foreperson of the jury, which returned a conviction.

A new trial has been ordered, and the prosecutor who failed to disclose the relationship has resigned.

It all comes back to integrity. Are the prosecutors playing games in order get a conviction or a favorable plea deal, or are the prosecutors committed to justice in whatever form it may take?

sports.title: Report: Giants DC Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview for Maryland head coaching job
sports.summary: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.
sports.body:
Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Wilson recently had a virtual interview with the University of Maryland. Maryland fired Mike Locksley last month after a 2-5 start to the season.

Wilson grew up in Maryland and played defensive back for the Terrapins. He was a graduate assistant at the school in 2007 and 2008 before embarking on an NFL career that has also included stints with the Rams, Jets, Eagles, Ravens and Titans.

Wilson is in his first year with the Giants. They rank 12th in points allowed and seventh in yards allowed this season.

sports.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker is not in concussion protocol
sports.summary: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.
sports.body:
Canales said at his press conference that Coker is not in concussion protocol as the Panthers move toward their Week 12 game against the Buccaneers.

Coker went for a check after taking a hit from Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith during the 35-33 Panthers win. He had four catches for 47 yards during the game.

Coker has 35 catches for 440 yards and three touchdowns on the season. He is second on the team in receptions behind fellow wideout Tetairoa McMillan.

sports.title: 49ers release WR Brandon Aiyuk
sports.summary: Aiyuk will next go to waivers.
sports.body:
Two weeks after 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk was reinstated from the reserve/left squad list, the 49ers have released him .

The 49ers had received a two-week roster exemption upon Aiyuk’s reinstatement. Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, the 49ers owed him no pay for the duration of the roster exemption.

He’ll now go to waivers, and he undoubtedly will be unclaimed. After that, he’ll become a free agent.

Many expect Aiyuk to sign with the Commanders, possibly with a practice-squad stint the first step back to the field.

Where he goes after that remains to be seen. Multiple contenders could use help at the position, if Aiyuk can perform like he did before the 2024 ACL tear that ultimately derailed his career.

sports.title: Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza: With two starts against two elite defenses, I've seen improvement
sports.summary: While Fernando Mendoza is still looking for his first win as a starting quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft displayed his considerable potential in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
sports.body:
Las Vegas was able to come back from down 17-0 to tie the game midway through the third quarter. Mendoza then engineered another touchdown drive midway through the fourth period to pull the Raiders within seven.

But the comeback effort ended when Mendoza threw a pick-six to Ja’Quan McMillian with just under two minutes left in regulation.

Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters on Monday that he saw Mendoza take steps in multiple areas.

“No. 1 is just the environment ,” Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. “That’s a very hostile environment, and I thought, overall, he did a good job of getting everybody on the same page. I thought he used his legs extremely well, extended some plays.

“For his second start in the NFL against two elite defenses, I’ve seen improvement.”

Kubiak also complimented Mendoza for the way he was able to bring the team back from being down 17.

“That’s who he is. That’s what he’s made of,” Kubiak said. “I think back to us being backed up, him taking a sack and then him making a really big third-down throw to Jack Bech. That’s what you need from your quarterback .”

Mendoza finished Sunday’s game 18-of-37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Mendoza’s next game will be his primetime debut, as the Raiders will face the Browns on Sunday night in Week 12.

sports.title: 49ers extend G.M. John Lynch's contract
sports.summary: In the offseason, the 49ers quietly extended the contract of coach Kyle Shanahan.
sports.body:
Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reports that the 49ers and G.M. John Lynch have agreed to a contract extension . Lynch, who also serves as the team’s president of football operations, was hired in early 2017. The Hall of Fame safety previously had worked for Fox.

Glazer explains that Lynch’s deal was due to expire after the 2026 season . Last night, Lynch and owner Jed York struck a handshake deal on a new contract before the Week 11 win over the Vikings.

With Shanahan and Lynch working together, the 49ers have qualified for a pair of Super Bowls. They have contended far more often than not, qualifying for the postseason in 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2025.

Before Shanahan and Lynch arrived, the 49ers hadn’t been to the playoffs since 2013.

This year, the 9-1 49ers have the inside track to the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoffs. They arguably have an excellent chance to win the franchise’s first Super Bowl since 1994.

sports.body: I think part of being a diehard NFL fan is trying to derive meaning out of everything that happens to a team, no matter how small. Think about the offseason program. How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second half of preseason games produce deep dive analysis of which players are potentially hidden gems or important depth pieces. Every now and then an OTA, training camp, or preseason, breakout turns out to be a preview of a genuine step forward by a developing player. Far more often the players and the hype are forgotten. It also goes this way in late season games when a team has fallen out of the Playoff race. Can a loss help a team secure a high Draft pick to land a franchise changing player? Can a late season surge lead to momentum carrying into a future season and be the first step in instilling a new culture? In both cases the answer is yes. Far more often, however, these games don’t have a ton of meaning either way in the long run. They amount to a bad team playing out the string. The Jets’ Week 11 victory over the Chargers has evoked passions across the fanbase. Some fans are furious about the team hurting its NFL Draft positioning. Others are happy to get the win. I don’t think there’s a “right” or a “wrong” way to be a fan. Everybody wants the same thing in the end, for the Jets to have success. Opinions simply vary on the best way to get there. I can understand fans who are hoping for as high of a pick as possible. Of course, we have seen over and over that the quality of the coaching staff and front office making the pick are generally far more important than where the pick is made. Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson were not the first quarterbacks selected in their respective Draft years. Taking it deeper, one study suggests the odds of the top player drafted at his position having a better career than the third player picked at the same position is only slightly better than a coin toss. Yes, there is the occasional case where losing helps a team land a player who legitimately changes everything, and there are cases where a meaningless late season win causes a team to miss out on that player. sports.body: OK, we have to talk about the Buffalo Bills electing to take the football to begin games this season. While it does seem to perfectly align with the aggressive vibe of the team’s head coach, let’s work to get as close as possible a determination of whether or not it’s a good idea for the Bills to be operating against the grain on this front. Now, of course, Buffalo can’t simply decide to take the football to begin each game. But Brady is electing to take it if his team wins the coin toss, and if the opponent wins it, it seems as though every other team will gladly defer to receiving the football at the start of the third quarter. Therefore, through 10 games, the Bills have been able to count on receiving the football to start the game. Earlier this season, I published two corresponding studies that examined how scoring right before the end of the half and “double-dipping” correlate to winning. I used a dataset that features all regular-season games from 2001 to 2025 and, at time of publication, the first three weeks of the 2026 season. This was the major finding from the first study: * Teams that outscored their opponent in the final two minutes went on to win 64.5% of the time And the biggest revelations from the second study on double-dipping, that matter here: * Teams that double dipped, which included a score of any kind, won at a 73.7% clip * Those double dips occurred in 13.6% of the games The last sentence I wrote: > “So, yes, teams should make a concerted effort to double dip. It correlates rather strongly with winning the football game.” And everyone would seemingly agree there, right? The double dip has become a phenomenon fans and media regularly mention as an objective teams should strive for in each game. The double dip is decently rare, something that happens in just a little under one out of every seven games. Part of the reason they don’t happen often because the double-dip opportunity only has about a coin-flip’s chance of materializing before halftime. Not necessarily because Allen always made the “right” decision determining at which level to throw the football. I want defenses to be forced to think about all possible variations of Buffalo’s offense. And Allen is the best player in football. The Bills slammed their foot on the gas pedal to begin this game, and while it didn’t amount to something like three-consecutive touchdown drives — which we’ve certainly witnessed during the Allen era — it led to three pass plays of 20-plus yards and two touchdowns in the first half as Buffalo built its lead. Allen seemed adamant about dicing the Dolphins secondary through the air, and not underneath. That is Allen being Allen. Allen didn’t have a carry against the Dolphins, which now amounts to, ironically, a similar place to where we were after the Patriots loss, when the Allen criticism centered around him throwing it downfield too frequently and not running nearly enough. And what happened after that? Allen averaged 11.1 yards per attempt and ran for 121 yards on 10 carries in a 37-34 win on the road against the Rams. The safety group has become a strength Amazing, right? Even if you don’t fully agree with me, it’s impossible it ignore the difference in the play of this group recently compared to the first month or so of the season. Cole Bishop is so perfectly positioned in his box/blitz role that asks him to cover the slot underneath. He’s become a weapon as an addition to the pass rush, and his size plus explosiveness and strength allow the Bills to defend the run respectably in dime, if needed. Good early returns on Amani Hooker, as he’s allowed four catches for 47 yards with two pass breakups, nine total tackles, and a quarterback hit on three pass-rush snaps in his two contests with the Bills. And, heck, new safety No. 3, Damar Hamlin, had the biggest splash play of the group against Miami, an impressive interception at the intermediate level. Jordan Hancock played outstandingly in the safety/slot hybrid role, and the Bills even got Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin Jr. onto the field in this contest.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills RB James Cook III makes NFL history in Week 11
sports.summary: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himsel
sports.body: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himself. With Sunday’s performance, which included 89 rushing yards and a touchdown, Cook became just the second player in NFL history to rush for at least 75 yards and score a rushing touchdown in nine consecutive games, moving past three former NFL running backs who had each reached eight straight. Notably, he’s the only player in league history to put up those numbers in one season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124605029529403539?a=SI4XCAzJ3357jRKxHXM&s=20] Cook entered the game tied with Pro Football Hall of Famers John Riggins and LaDainian Tomlinson, along with George Rogers, for the second-longest streak in NFL history. Riggins accomplished the feat in 1983, Rogers did it across the 1985 and 1986 seasons, and Tomlinson matched them in 2006. The 27-year-old Cook joined that group during Buffalo’s Week 10 victory over the New York Jets. He rushed for 157 yards on 18 carries, including a career-long 74-yard touchdown run in the second half of the Bills’ 31-12 win. Now, only Terry Allen stands ahead of Cook. Allen reached 10 consecutive games with at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown while playing for Washington across the 1995 and 1996 seasons. With nine straight games behind him, Cook is now within striking distance of a record that’s stood for 30 years, but the road won’t get any easier. Kansas City and New England are next on Buffalo’s schedule, and the dates next to those names are just as challenging as the opponents. The Bills have just three days to rest, recover, and prepare to host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. If Cook is going to catch Terry Allen, he’ll have to keep his streak alive through one of the toughest stretches of Buffalo’s season.

sports.body: Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has reinvented himself this year. A new position, a new number, new coaches and an entirely new defensive scheme. And the results? Is it too early to start throwing around the word legendary? Maybe, but Rousseau is certainly making a case for it. With two sacks against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Rousseau has officially entered uncharted territory in his NFL career. His 10 sacks this season are a new personal best. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124568810426356152?a=PKP5mAXAD9DcankXAG0&s=20] Rousseau sacked Miami quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss that forced the Dolphins to punt after a five-play first drive. Then in the second quarter, it was an almost identical play. Rousseau dropped McCord for another eight-yard loss. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124585141821452485?a=LnRiXda6MHK5TN5rwfs&s=20] Rousseau entered the NFL in 2021 as a defensive end, spending his first five seasons in Sean McDermott’s defensive system. Along the way, he worked under Leslie Frazier, McDermott himself, and Bobby Babich as defensive leaders, while learning from defensive line coaches Eric Washington and Marcus West. Then came 2026, and just about everything changed. Jim Leonhard took over as defensive coordinator, bringing a new scheme that moved Rousseau from defensive end to outside linebacker. Bobby April III became his new position coach, giving Rousseau his third position coach and fourth defensive leader in six NFL seasons. Somehow, through all that change, Rousseau is putting together the most productive season of his career. He recorded four sacks as a rookie in 2021, eight in 2022, five in 2023, eight again in 2024 and seven last season. Those eight-sack performances had been his personal best until Sunday. Of course, Rousseau didn’t exactly ease into his new role — he came roaring in right from the start. He opened the season with three consecutive two-sack games, becoming the first player in Bills history to accomplish that feat. Only two other players in NFL history had ever done it. sports.body: It’s a beautiful victory, Monday, New York Jets fans! I’m sure everyone is happy about this dub, right? Wrong. The fan base is fractured down the middle with this result. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what they describe as a frustrating loss to a crappy opponent that screwed up their draft positioning. “A Jets win that feels like a loss to many people in the fan base, and I don’t blame anyone who feels that way because I feel the same way. Watching the Jets go out there and win this game just leaves that sinking feeling in your stomach oh my God they have ruined the tank again. That’s the feeling many in the fan base have, and if you feel that way, you’re not a bad fan because you see the forest through the trees because you understand that a win over a one-win Chargers team could potentially do more damage than good. If you’re going to win games, you want it to be because your young players are playing great, not because 33-year-old Sterling Shepard is scoring two touchdowns on his only two touches of the game,” ESPN New York’s Jake Asman lamented. The Jets were not going to finish 2-15. Anyone who set that expectation set themselves up for failure. They have been in a ton of close games this season. A broken clock is right twice a day. A blind squirrel can find a nut. The Jets were eventually going to stumble into a victory, and who knows if this is the last one. There are still six games left in the 2026 regular season. For fans who like seeing their green and white team win regardless of circumstance, cheers to you today. We’ve only had three wins this year; enjoy them while you can. --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: The New York Jets broke a five game losing streak and got their third win of the season on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Jets are now 3-8 on the season, in third place in the AFC East. The Jets scored on the opening drive of the game and never looked back. The Jets never trailed in the game. They scored every time they had the ball other than their last possession, when they ran out the clock to seal the win. The Jets offense bullied the Chargers defense all day. The running game was efficient and effective. The Jets converted on better than 80% of their third downs. Geno Smith was accurate and efficient, spreading the ball around effectively. Practice squad call-up Sterling Shepard scored twice. It was a really nice offensive performance by the Jets. Defensively the Jets struggled, but David Bailey got another two sacks to get to 9.5 for the season and the offense was good enough to get the victory. The win over the Chargers left the Jets with a 3-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 1-9 Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins’ only win this season came at the expense of the Jets a few weeks ago. Since the Dolphins’ victory over the Jets in October the Dolphins lost three straight competitive games to the New England Patriots, Detroit Lions and Indianapolis Colts before getting blown out this Sunday by the Buffalo Bills. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The oddsmakers think the Jets will beat the Dolphins next Sunday. The current line has the Jets road favorites by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 41.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are -215 while the Dolphins are +180. A win against the Dolphins next Sunday would send the Jets going into their Week 13 bye with some momentum and a chance to finish the season on the upswing. sports.body: In the immediate aftermath of the Buffalo Bills’ Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins, many will scratch their heads wondering what they watched unfold Sunday afternoon. To be clear her: What a strange win by the Bills. Buffalo’s offense barely resembled the group most have watched in 2026. It’s important to step back a moment, however, and realize that Buffalo has built a good, often great team. The Bills haven’t trailed in a game since October 18 against the Las Vegas Raiders (hat tip: Carson Hayek). Buffalo has also won three consecutive games by 17 or more points. What about the defense? Well, that group hasn’t allowed a touchdown in three straight games. It may be true that the Bills didn’t execute their most impressive game plan of the season, and that they strayed too far away from their true identity until crunch time. It’s clear that quarterback Josh Allen didn’t have his typically dominant effort against the Dolphins, even though he did throw for 304 yards, but he didn’t need to play lights out. Interestingly, Allen attempted zero rushes. In fact, during a first-half 4th & 1 situation, Allen handed the ball off to running back James Cook III, who scampered through the right side of the line to move the chains. The intent seemed clear that the move was to avoid exposing Allen to unnecessary contact, at least. That move can only work so well when you ask the quarterback to drop back 45 times. As a result, Miami’s defense hit Allen six times, sacking him on three occasions. Most believed that Buffalo would use their dominant rushing attack to try and wear down the Dolphins’ trio of backup defensive tackles in the first half. It was tough sledding early, perhaps surprisingly to Brady and the offense, and Cook had just 13 carries for 36 yards and a touchdown at halftime. Allen was forced into two consecutive interceptions late in the second quarter, with a third erased due to penalty. Then consider the decisions on special teams.
